title: Degree adverbs: very, too, extremely, quite
summary: Наречия степени: градуальные и неградуальные прилагательные (**very good / absolutely wonderful**), смыслы **quite / rather / pretty / fairly**, **too, enough, so, such** и усиление глаголов (**very much, really**).
ru:
## Градуальные и неградуальные прилагательные
Градуальные прилагательные имеют степени — «немного/очень» (**good, tired, cold, interesting**). Неградуальные выражают крайнее или абсолютное значение (**fantastic, exhausted, impossible, freezing, unique, perfect**). От этого зависит, какое наречие подходит.
- с градуальными: **very, extremely, really, rather, fairly, pretty, a bit, slightly, terribly, awfully**
- с неградуальными: **absolutely, completely, totally, utterly, really, quite**
> The film was **very good** / **absolutely brilliant**. — Фильм был очень хорош / просто блестящий.
> I was **extremely tired** / **completely exhausted**. — Я ужасно устал / абсолютно измотан.
- ~~very fantastic~~, ~~absolutely good~~, ~~completely tired~~ (в нейтральной речи) → **absolutely fantastic**, **very good**, **very tired**.
Исключение: **really** сочетается и с теми, и с другими: *really good, really fantastic*.

## quite: два смысла
У **quite** два разных значения. С градуальным прилагательным в британском английском оно значит «довольно, умеренно»; с неградуальным — «совершенно, абсолютно».
> The food was **quite good**. (BrE) — Еда была вполне ничего (не отлично).
> She is **quite right** / **quite impossible**. — Она совершенно права / совершенно невозможна.
В американском английском **quite** чаще значит «очень», а умеренное значение передаёт **pretty** и **fairly**.
Порядок: **quite a** + прилагательное + существительное; ~~a quite good singer~~ → **quite a good singer**.

## fairly, rather, pretty
- **fairly** — умеренно-положительно: *fairly good*, *fairly easy*.
- **rather** — сильнее; часто с неприятным или неожиданным оттенком: *rather late*, *rather expensive*, но *rather good* — приятное удивление.
- **pretty** — разговорное, близко к «довольно»: *pretty cold*.
- **a bit / a little / slightly** — слабая степень; обычно о негативном: *a bit tired*. Перед существительным не ставятся.
> It's **rather late**; we should leave. — Уже поздновато, нам пора.

## too, enough, so, such
- **too** = больше, чем нужно (проблема): *too heavy to lift*. **much / far / way too** усиливает; **very** не нужен.
- **enough** ставится **после** прилагательного/наречия и **перед** существительным: *big enough*, *enough chairs*.
- **so** + прилагательное/наречие, **such** + (a/an) + прилагательное + существительное:
> It was **so** hot. / It was **such a** hot day. — Было так жарко. / Был такой жаркий день.
> ~~such hot~~, ~~so a hot day~~ → **so hot**, **such a hot day**
> The test was **so difficult that** nobody finished. — Тест был настолько труден, что никто не закончил.

## Усиление глаголов
С глаголами используют **very much, really, greatly, thoroughly, deeply**. **Very** без much с глаголом нельзя.
> I **really** enjoyed it. / I **very much** enjoyed it. / I enjoyed it **very much**.
- ~~I very enjoyed the concert.~~ → I **very much** enjoyed it.
- **hardly, scarcely, barely** — «едва»: *I can hardly breathe.* (уже отрицательные)

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She is very exhausted.~~ → She is **absolutely/completely** exhausted. (или **very tired**)
- ~~It's enough big.~~ → It's **big enough**.
- ~~We were such tired.~~ → We were **so tired**.
- ~~He is very too young.~~ → He is **much too** young.
en:
## Gradable and non-gradable adjectives
Gradable adjectives have degrees — 'a little / very' (**good, tired, cold, interesting**). Non-gradable adjectives express an extreme or absolute meaning (**fantastic, exhausted, impossible, freezing, unique, perfect**). This decides which adverb fits.
- with gradable: **very, extremely, really, rather, fairly, pretty, a bit, slightly, terribly, awfully**
- with non-gradable: **absolutely, completely, totally, utterly, really, quite**
> The film was **very good** / **absolutely brilliant**.
> I was **extremely tired** / **completely exhausted**.
- ~~very fantastic~~, ~~absolutely good~~, ~~completely tired~~ (in neutral usage) → **absolutely fantastic**, **very good**, **very tired**.
Exception: **really** combines with both: *really good, really fantastic*.

## quite: two meanings
**quite** has two meanings. With a gradable adjective in British English it means 'fairly, moderately'; with a non-gradable adjective it means 'completely'.
> The food was **quite good**. (BrE: good, but not excellent)
> She is **quite right** / **quite impossible**.
In American English **quite** more often means 'very', and the moderate sense is expressed by **pretty** and **fairly**.
Order: **quite a** + adjective + noun; ~~a quite good singer~~ → **quite a good singer**.

## fairly, rather, pretty
- **fairly** — moderately positive: *fairly good*, *fairly easy*.
- **rather** — stronger; often negative or surprising: *rather late*, *rather expensive*, but *rather good* is a pleasant surprise.
- **pretty** — informal, close to 'rather': *pretty cold*.
- **a bit / a little / slightly** — a small degree; usually about negative things: *a bit tired*. They are not used before a noun.
> It's **rather late**; we should leave.

## too, enough, so, such
- **too** = more than necessary (a problem): *too heavy to lift*. **much / far / way too** strengthens it; **very** is not needed.
- **enough** goes **after** an adjective/adverb and **before** a noun: *big enough*, *enough chairs*.
- **so** + adjective/adverb, **such** + (a/an) + adjective + noun:
> It was **so** hot. / It was **such a** hot day.
> ~~such hot~~, ~~so a hot day~~ → **so hot**, **such a hot day**
> The test was **so difficult that** nobody finished.

## Strengthening verbs
With verbs use **very much, really, greatly, thoroughly, deeply**. **Very** alone cannot modify a verb.
> I **really** enjoyed it. / I **very much** enjoyed it. / I enjoyed it **very much**.
- ~~I very enjoyed the concert.~~ → I **very much** enjoyed it.
- **hardly, scarcely, barely** — 'almost not': *I can hardly breathe.* (already negative)

## Common mistakes
- ~~She is very exhausted.~~ → She is **absolutely/completely** exhausted. (or **very tired**)
- ~~It's enough big.~~ → It's **big enough**.
- ~~We were such tired.~~ → We were **so tired**.
- ~~He is very too young.~~ → He is **much too** young.
structure:
## Подбор наречия
| Тип прилагательного | Наречия | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Градуальное | very, extremely, really, rather, fairly | **very** cold, **extremely** useful |
| Неградуальное | absolutely, completely, totally, utterly | **absolutely** freezing, **utterly** impossible |
| Оба | really, quite (разное значение) | **really** good / **really** fantastic |

## Формулы
> **quite a / such a / rather a / what a** + (adj) + существительное: **quite a** surprise
> **too** + adj/adv (+ **for** + кто-то) + **to**-инфинитив: **too** tired **to** drive
> adj/adv + **enough** (+ **for** ... / **to** ...): clever **enough to** understand
> **enough** + существительное: **enough** time
> **so** + adj/adv + **that**; **such (a)** + adj + сущ. + **that**
> глагол: **very much / really + verb**; **hardly / barely + verb**

## Сравнение: оттенки силы
| Слабее | Умеренно | Сильнее |
|---|---|---|
| a bit, slightly | fairly, quite (BrE), pretty | very, extremely, terribly, **absolutely** (нгр.) |

exercises.title: Подберите наречие степени
exercises.instruction: Вставьте одно слово по смыслу. Если возможны синонимы — они учтены.

items.text: The view from the top was {{absolutely|utterly|simply}} breathtaking.
She was {{very|really|extremely}} tired after the long flight.
The soup is {{too}} salty to eat.
Is the water warm {{enough}} for swimming?
He is {{much|far}} too young to drive.
It was {{such}} a boring film that we left early.
The film was {{so}} boring that we left early.
He isn't experienced {{enough}} for the job.
It was {{such}} a long journey that we all fell asleep.
The tea was {{so}} hot that I couldn't drink it.
The test was {{too}} difficult for most students.
They were {{so}} kind to us during our stay.
She is not tall {{enough}} to reach the top shelf.

items.q: The room isn't ___ for ten people.
It was ___ a good idea that everyone agreed.

items.why: С глаголом — **very much**, не просто very.

items.q: He's ___ too young to understand this.

items.why: Верно **quite a good singer**: quite стоит перед артиклем a.
С градуальным прилагательным в BrE quite = умеренная степень.

items.q: The room was ___ small for all of us.
She was absolutely ___ to hear the news.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя **too, enough** или **so ... that**.

items.prompt: The box is so heavy that I can't lift it. → The box is too heavy ...
answers: The box is too heavy for me to lift.
The box is too heavy to lift.

items.prompt: She isn't old enough to vote. → She is ...
answers: She is too young to vote.
She's too young to vote.

items.prompt: He's so tired that he can't concentrate. → He's ...
answers: He's too tired to concentrate.
He is too tired to concentrate.

items.prompt: The room is too small for twenty people. → The room isn't ...
answers: The room isn't big enough for twenty people.
The room isn't large enough for twenty people.
The room is not big enough for twenty people.
The room is not large enough for twenty people.

items.prompt: It was such a difficult question that nobody answered. → The question was so difficult ...
answers: The question was so difficult that nobody answered it.
The question was so difficult that nobody answered.

items.prompt: The coffee was too hot to drink. → The coffee was so hot ...
answers: The coffee was so hot that I couldn't drink it.
The coffee was so hot that I could not drink it.
The coffee was so hot I couldn't drink it.
The coffee was so hot I could not drink it.

exercises.title: Переведите на английский
exercises.instruction: Переведите на английский, используя слова в скобках.

answers: The film was absolutely fantastic.
The movie was absolutely fantastic.

items.prompt: Он слишком молод, чтобы водить машину.
answers: He is too young to drive.
He's too young to drive.
He is too young to drive a car.
He's too young to drive a car.

items.prompt: Она достаточно умна, чтобы понять это. (clever)
answers: She is clever enough to understand.
She's clever enough to understand.
She is clever enough to understand it.
She's clever enough to understand it.
She is clever enough to understand this.
She's clever enough to understand this.

items.prompt: Это была такая скучная лекция, что я заснул. (such)
answers: It was such a boring lecture that I fell asleep.
It was such a boring lecture I fell asleep.
That was such a boring lecture that I fell asleep.
That was such a boring lecture I fell asleep.
I really enjoyed the concert.
I very much enjoyed the concert.
I enjoyed the concert very much.
I enjoyed the concert a lot.
I really liked the concert.
I liked the concert very much.
I liked the concert a lot.
I very much liked the concert.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя наречия степени.

items.prompt: Describe something that you found absolutely amazing or awful recently.
items.sample: The sunrise over the lake last weekend was absolutely stunning.

items.prompt: Describe your job or studies using quite / rather / fairly.
items.sample: My job is fairly demanding, but the people are rather friendly.

items.prompt: Write about something that is too difficult or too expensive for you right now.
items.sample: A new car is far too expensive for me at the moment.
I'm not fit enough to run a marathon.
